name: Mindo Village
tagline: The three-street centre, hostels and the tour operators
description: The village itself, essentially three streets with hostels, small restaurants, the chocolate operation and the guides who take people out at dawn to look for birds. Everything is walkable, the connectivity is the best in the valley, and it is the only place with any services.
bestFor: Anyone who needs a shop, a restaurant and a guide within a two-minute walk
pros: The only services, shops and restaurants in the area
The best connectivity in the valley
Guides, tubing and the chocolate tour all here
cons: Highest rates in the area, though still very low
Busy with weekend visitors from Quito

name: Rio Mindo and the Waterfall Road
tagline: Up the valley towards the cable car and the falls
description: The road climbing east out of the village along the river towards the tarabita cable car and the chain of waterfalls beyond it. Lodges and cabins sit among the forest on both sides, with hummingbird feeders on every terrace and the trails starting at the door.
bestFor: Stays that want the waterfalls and the forest trails immediately accessible
pros: Waterfall trails and the cable car nearby
River running past and complete quiet
cons: A vehicle or a long walk into the village
Very wet, with mud on the trails year-round

name: Nambillo and the Southern Slopes
tagline: The forest reserves above the village
description: The slopes south and west of Mindo where several private reserves protect cloud forest and run their own trail networks and feeder stations. Accommodation is lodges rather than village rooms, and this is where the serious birdwatching happens, at dawn and in silence.
bestFor: Birdwatchers, for whom this is the whole reason the place exists
pros: Private reserves with dedicated trails and hides
The best birding density in the valley
Cloud forest immediately outside the door
cons: Lodge pricing rather than village pricing

name: Mindo Road and the Nono Corridor
tagline: The old road up towards the paramo and Quito
description: The route climbing east out of the valley towards Nono and eventually Quito, passing through successive forest bands as the altitude rises, with scattered lodges known among birders for the species that change every few hundred metres of climb.
bestFor: Stays that want the altitude gradient and the birding it produces
pros: Distinct bird communities at each elevation band
On the road back to Quito
cons: A vehicle is essential and the road is slow
Twenty to thirty minutes from Mindo village

name: San Miguel de los Bancos (20 km west)
tagline: The market town down the valley, lower and warmer
description: A working town twenty kilometres west and several hundred metres lower, with a market, banks, a hospital and none of the tourism that shapes Mindo. It is warmer, cheaper and entirely practical, and it is where people in the valley go for anything they cannot buy locally.
bestFor: Long stays needing real services and the lowest costs in the area
pros: The lowest costs in the valley
cons: Twenty to thirty minutes from Mindo
No cloud forest and no birding infrastructure
An ordinary town with nothing to see
